# 08 · The Tall Hearth
Population as the multiplier; the guilds are the passive late act, spending citizens the
active one. Wins by: The Metropolis · The Greatest City · The Census of the World.

## Æra I
- Tech:
  - Agriculture — unlocks Settler, Warrior, Scout, Worker, Farm
  - Earthenware — unlocks Granary
- Orders:
  - Granary Levies (the growth trigger — multiply this shape)
  - Public Granaries — Cities keep 25% of their stored food when they grow.
  - Hearth Songs — +1 culture in every city of 4 population or less.
  - Festival Days — +4 happiness.
- Religion:
  - Goddess of the Harvest — +1 food on every hex carrying a bonus resource that pays food.
  - Keeper of the Hearth — Granaries supply +1 faith. +1 happiness in the capital.
  - River Mother — +2 food in every city on fresh water. Those cities' shrines supply +1 happiness.
- Wonders:
  - The Hanging Gardens — +25% food surplus stored toward growth · +1 food on every hex with a Farm beside fresh water, in every city with The Hanging Gardens
- Deeds:
  - The Breadbasket — Keep one city fed to a hundred of food for ten turns together.

## Æra II
- Orders:
  - The Grain Dole — +2 happiness in every city of 6 or more population.
  - Scholars' Stipend (✶ crossover) — +2 science in every city of 5 or more population.
  - Toleration Edicts — −10% happiness demanded per citizen.
- Doctrines:
  - River Kings — +30% food in every city on fresh water; −10% food and −10% production in every city without it.
  - The Hermit Crown — While you hold at most 4 cities: +30% to every yield in your capital.
  - The Gentle Yoke — −15% happiness demanded per citizen · every city costs 2 more authority.
  - The Scattered Hearths — The first 3 citizens in every city demand no happiness · −4 happiness in your capital.
- Religion:
  - Common Table — A city that follows keeps a quarter of its stored food when it grows.
  - Choirs — +1 culture for every 3 citizens of a city that follows.
  - Feast Days — +1 happiness for every city that follows, and +1 more for each with a Temple.
  - Tithe Houses — +1 gold for every 4 citizens of a city that follows.
- Systems: the guilds open (renown → specialists)
- Deeds:
  - The Metropolis — Grow a city to twenty citizens.
  - The Census of the World — A race. Needs a city of fifteen citizens. The first empire to finish gains a citizen in every city.

## Æra III
- Tech: Engineering (existing Æra III node) — the Aqueduct's home: the growth marquee as a plain building unlock, with Mathematics beside it for the tall-science lean.
- Orders: ▢ ________ (a growth-trigger III: when a city grows, X — Granary Levies' big sibling)
- Doctrines:
  - Pax Imperia — +3 happiness and +3 culture in every city of 8 or more population.
  - Pax Magistri — +3 happiness in every city. +5 science and +5 culture in every city of 12 or more population.
  - The Yeomanry — +1 production on every hex with a Farm. Cities of 10 or more population −1 happiness.
  - The Wandering Court — −15% to every yield in your capital · +3 food, production, science, culture and faith, and +3 happiness, in every city but your capital.
- Governments:
  - Republic — +1 culture for each 5 population in a city. −5% happiness demanded per citizen.
  - The Estates — +1 happiness in every city. +2 culture in every city of 8 or more population.
- Buildings: *(planned)* the physicians' college (surplus food → science)
- Deeds:
  - The Greatest City — At the close of the age, the empire holding the largest city.

## Æra IV
- Orders: *(planned)* specialist consumption — an artist's masterwork, a scholar's treatise (spend a specialist for a lump + legacy)
- Projects: *(planned)* The Great Levy (−1 population → hammers, repeatable)
- Deeds: ▢ ________ · Opus: any pillar, by sheer output

## Gaps
The III growth marquee; crowding relief is the Core posture's budget and must be an
Order/government line under the new ruling, not a building parade.
